item.title: Podcast: Three Money Myths Students Believe
item.summary: A student money podcast takes apart three common beliefs about budgeting, small purchases and saving.
item.transcript_text: Hi everyone, and welcome back to Pocket Money, the podcast about managing money when you don't have much of it. Today I want to bust three money myths that I hear from students all the time. Myth number one: budgeting is only for people with a lot of money. Actually, it's the opposite. When your income is small, every decision matters more, so knowing where your money goes is even more important. Myth number two: small purchases don't count. A coffee here, a taxi there, it doesn't feel like much. But if you write down everything you spend for just one week, you'll probably be surprised by how quickly those little things add up. Now, I'm not saying never buy coffee. I'm saying make it a choice, not a habit. Myth number three: you can start saving later, once you have a proper job. The amount you save as a student might be tiny, and that's completely fine. What you're really building is the habit. One simple trick is to move a small, fixed amount into a separate account on the day your stipend or salary arrives, before you have time to spend it. Pay yourself first, as people say. So, here's this week's challenge: track every single purchase for seven days, and then send me your biggest surprise. See you next time!
